obligations.description: **Choose the first boundary:** retained regular-file capability + bounded reads, p11scope and OSSLscope as design donors, with two real standalone reference clients for initial acceptance. Architecture owner.
**Refresh selected donor state**, including applicable WIP. Integration owner.
**Set package license, dependency and compiler policy.** Maintainer.
**Create `docs/issues/` and an operational regression index.** Test/documentation owner.
**Define evidence labels for tests and support.** Test owner.
**Select names after review.** Maintainer.
**Evaluate dependencies before extracting parsers:** procfs + rustix/nix; object/goblin; optional pathrs/blazesym and cap-std/cap-tempfile for held directory/fixture operations. Linux-library owner.

**Define the selected authority/identity types.** First slice: held regular-file capability and stat/read evidence; narrow process-observation authority only if acquisition needs it. Record separate future contracts for control handles, exec generation, mapped-device identity and stronger content/image evidence.
**Carry retained-file and bounded-read regressions.** Library + both consumer owners.
**Deliver filesystem-domain behavior and independent fixtures for the ready maps-proof adapter.** Library/test owners.
**Separate observer and owned-child authority.** Linux-library owner.
**Audit process-global integration hazards before adding helper supervision.** Linux-library owner.
**Later MG01/MG02: migrate first two products and retire their old implementation.** p11scope/OSSLscope owners.
**Generalize discovery budgets after the qualified identity slice.** Library owner.
**Specify restart behavior.** Architecture owner.
**Consolidate exact per-CPU map geometry.** BPF-library owner.
**Separate attachment planning from loading.** BPF-library + two uprobe consumers.
**Share feature/hazard result types.** BPF-library owner.
**Trial an existing BTF parser against donor corpus.** BTF owner.
**Create one upstream-patch register and reproducible patch application path.** Dependency owner.
**Re-evaluate Aya/local-map relocation against a chosen upstream release.** Dependency owner.
**Define bounded ring consumption without overstating settlement.** Transport owner.
**Document writer ownership per hook/program/CPU and architecture.** Producer owner.
**Evaluate shared task/exec identity protocol as a separate design.** Identity owner.
**Select an initial kernel/architecture support matrix.** Maintainers.
**Recover the LLVM/BPF instruction and atomic regression cases.** Compiler/test owner.
**Replace a bare CPU-preset assumption with an explicit instruction contract.** Compiler owner.
**Track upstream atomic fix through consumer toolchains.** Dependency owner.
**Preserve actual-object checks for verifier-sensitive changes.** Compiler/test owner.
**Extract safe nested-build helpers if needed.** Build owner.
**Create a compatibility cookbook with workaround expiration rules.** Documentation/compiler owner.
**Design loss/provenance types and units.** Capture-library owner.
**Preserve report-view isolation.** Capture-library owner.
**Specify closure strength and late evidence.** Capture/producer owners.
**Conformance tests for two independent real reference consumers before freezing types.** Capture/test owners; OSSLscope/KryProbe/MemVeil provide contract cases.
**Strict replay/schema checks.** Capture/test owner.
**Evaluate cross-stage resource reservations after selecting accepted donor code.** General Rust/capture owner.
**Maintain the 32-family regression inventory and port selected cases.** Test owner.
**Add property/model tests where they detect distinct bugs.** Library/test owners.
**Add oracle sensitivity, non-vacuity and harness controls.** Test owner.
**Exercise cancellation/resource exhaustion and concurrent consumers.** Integration owner.
**Wire dependency-aware CI.** Build/test owner.
**Verify standalone consumers and performance budgets.** Integration owner.
**Check documentation/API claims for drift.** Documentation owner.
Choose positional full-file versus explicit stream/range semantics. **P0 pilot/public file.**
Declare proc-fd dependency; typed refusal, no path reopen fallback. **P0 affected file/attach.**
Structured stage/source/effect errors and caller retry policy. **P0 public operations.**
Separate byte/work/wait/cleanup bounds. **P0 byte/time claims.**
Define peak/retained/working memory and allocation-failure policy. **P0 memory-bound claims.**
Encapsulate evidence/FD; define borrow, clone, escape and CLOEXEC. **P0 public file.**
Define cancellation commit/result/custody semantics. **P1 async/deadline.**
Explicit close receipt, Drop policy, bounded quarantine admission. **P1 retirement.**
Specify panic/poison behavior without promising abort recovery. **P0 public callbacks, P1 later adapters.**
Declare auto-traits, same-owner concurrency and reentrancy. **P0 public owners.**
Separate caller fork/exec from observed target lifecycle. **P0 FD inheritance, P1 worker fork.**
Scope receipts and cache invalidation to object/context/operation. **P0 exported cached evidence, P1 added BPF profile.**
Document permissions and parent-state effects; no implicit privilege policy. **P1 process/BPF/helper.**
Negotiate minimum semantics before admission/effects. **P1 fallback profiles.**
Define imported/shared map/link/cursor ownership. **P1 advertised coexistence.**
Define sample epoch, reset, wrap and non-atomicity. **P1 sampled capture counters.**
Type clock domains, conversion, failure and suspend behavior. **P1 timestamps/deadlines.**
Write checked safe-backend pre/postconditions and trust boundaries. **P0 public reader/budget, P1 backends.**
Define additive features/public dependency types. **P0 Rust package composition.**
Set Rust/error/receipt/vector/MSRV compatibility policy. **P0 public API evolution.**
Separate host tools, generated target and runtime profile/environment. **P2 build/object profiles.**
Opt-in bounded sink, safe display, structured sensitive fields. **P0 public diagnostics.**
Stage baseline/config/links/readiness/admission explicitly. **P1 capture startup.**
**Define the ready mapped-image contract and support profiles.**
**Implement explicit mapping evidence and validity rules.**
**Ship the embeddable conformance API and immutable case/fixture versions.**
**Ship a runnable operator route and complete offline fixture closure.**
**Provide real filesystem/namespace fixtures and provisioning recipes.**
**Qualify effects, interference, cleanup and harness sensitivity.**
**Version result schema and enforce complete-profile verdicts.**
**Maintain qualified cells and usable end-user documentation.**
Compose a thin `scopebase-sdk`, a non-crypto host observer and an opt-in real BPF observer.
Evaluate general shared CLI/build/report integration only where demonstrated.
Define neutral scenario/schema fragments for Rust/C/Mojo.
Evaluate existing libbpf-mojo before any new native bridge.
Coordinate future MojoBPF object/ABI conformance.
Add a C ABI only for a demonstrated second-language need.
Successful exec advances image lineage; fork and thread creation have distinct identity effects.
Acquisition races and denied pidfd never retarget authority or promote weak observation to signaling rights.
Session/map domains and generations reject foreign/stale/exhausted tokens while preserving field-specific valid zero.
Replacement, unlink and aliases do not retarget a held file; attachment retains its original file through retirement.
Stat, mount, namespace and maps identities remain tagged; mappings require justified match, mismatch or inconclusive evidence.
Reads reject oversize before expensive allocation and expose promised growth, truncation, identity and budget failures.
Local section-symbol relocation resolves each exact map definition and rejects interior, missing or ambiguous offsets.
Task-storage metadata, guarded CO-RE shapes and initialized padding admit only safe compiled paths.
Concurrent uprobes never observe another task START key; workaround removal is qualified per kernel cell.
Object graph transformations preserve valid calls, callback metadata and exact intended callback execution.
Bounded BTF queries resolve exact base/split type identities and reject cycles, escapes and wrong prototypes/linkage.
Bounded ring consumption handles busy/discard/wrap and fixed boundaries without claiming premature completion.
Held ring bytes survive short retry/source mutation and are delivered once with disjoint transport accounting.
Writer slots protect same-CPU cross-program and guarded same-program updates; refusals have independent miss accounting.
Insertion identity stays frozen across CPU migration and every per-CPU ABI lane is consumed at the correct stride.
Per-CPU buffers use checked aligned value stride times possible CPUs, preserving offline lanes or refusing malformed topology.
Loss signaling survives full identity maps and caps degrade exactness without fabricating omitted counts.
Final settlement requires declared admission, writer, drain and post-drain sample predicates; late work invalidates early closure.
Pending/failed retirement keeps original owner/file; foreign tickets and failed transfers cannot settle it.
Stalled setup and late publishers have bounded caller cancellation while preserving successor output and foreign-process authority.
Attach isolation is bounded by 2n-1 attempts and permission/exhaustion policy preserves explicit partial-effect rollback.
Capability evidence requires independently executed admitted positives and active excluded negatives.
Strict receipt parsing rejects malformed, ambiguous or contradictory records before evidence promotion.
Checked construction and replay enforce the same identity, scope arithmetic, interval and synthetic-provenance invariants.
Unknown identities do not collide and old-generation completions cannot retire reused successor objects.
Independent facts survive missing relationships; alternate totals never double-count the same work.
Snapshots are non-destructive; ordered metrics require their proof and late corrections reach every holder.
Native retained views, buffers and loader lifetimes enforce generation, map-kind, output and exactly-once destruction rules.
Used-result atomic RMW returns the independently expected old value and stores the expected new value through the final consumer build.
Compiler upgrades cannot emit instructions outside an explicitly selected advertised profile even when CPU preset names are unchanged.
AtomicLoad instruction selection compiles or refuses under its declared CPU/features without being mislabeled as a kernel failure.
Mixed Rust/C debug-record transformations preserve valid final BTF/BTF.ext function and map information.
Process handle vs signaling authority
Producer task birth and exec image identity
Held image/file and attach lifetime
Stat-device vs maps-device identity
Bounded file/proc parsing and reads
BTF required layout/prototype admission
Possible-CPU count and checked map buffer extent
Map-kind-sensitive output semantics
Multi-uprobes and bounded failure isolation
Functional kernel feature/hazard diagnosis
Bounded ring cursor/frame consumption
Admission → writer quiescence → final sample
Cross-program same-CPU writer isolation
Loss indication survives full producer maps
Loss/counters retain units, scope and ownership
Explicit unknown vs valid numeric zero
Generations, reuse and late completion
Causal origin distinct from execution context
Nonduplicating ambiguity and alternative views
Query-local partial vs persistent degradation
Ordered interval peak/occupancy proof
Scope partition/live-replay invariants
Batch versus live session conformance
Finite child cleanup and output custody
Toolchain pairing and build-output isolation
Actual-object/verifier/relocation regressions
Strict numeric/schema/receipt validation
Reusable cross-language ownership ABI
Keep author-authorized source/destination grants and target input options separate from final object/runtime license bytes and intended-reason kernel admission.

Inspect actual final ELF declaration and manifest binding
Valid GPL positive with nonempty independent workload; otherwise-valid non-GPL intended-reason refusal; helper-free control where supported; same-errno permission/verifier negatives remain distinct
